Cathy White

Working Class candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Maryland · Challenger

Factory production worker

Cathy White is the Working Class Party's nominee for Governor of Maryland, and Cathy Permut is her running mate for Lieutenant Governor. The party nominated them at its state convention in April 2026. The party qualified for the 2026 ballot by turning in more than 12,000 signatures to the Board of Elections. White says she has worked in a factory as a production worker for 40 years and describes herself as not a professional politician.

Where White stands

Affordability / cost of living
Says low wages, inflation, high prices and a lack of jobs are workers' main problems, and that people can't afford to live anywhere.
Health care
Says childcare and eldercare cost more than most workers can afford. She cites her own experience caring for her mother and her sister while working full time.
Economy and jobs
Says employers are cutting workers and making the remaining ones do more work. Says young workers can't find jobs, gig workers get no benefits, and many older workers cannot afford to retire.
Elections / two-party system
Argues that both major parties serve billionaires. Supports workers building their own political organization, separate from unions and reaching across all industries.
Immigration
Says she rejects attacks on immigrants and other groups, and argues those attacks divide and weaken workers.
Transportation and infrastructure
Says schools are run-down, roads and bridges are falling apart, and sewage pipes are breaking.
Energy costs / foreign policy
Opposes the current U.S. war in the Middle East. Says defense contractors and oil and gas companies benefit from it while workers pay more for gas.

Background

  • Working Class Party nominee for Governor of Maryland, 2026 (nominated at the party's April 2026 convention)
  • Factory production worker for about 40 years (her own description); WYPR's 2022 voter guide described her as a former photofinishing factory worker
  • No public office held
